title: Where and how do you get assets for your game
author: Basic_Construction98
selftext:
After opus 5.5 got out it feels like there was a huge jump in 3d but still it feels like the assets and animations are very basic.

I see here people show games with amazing graphics an i assume they are also made with ai

 Is there a good workflow with ai services that do it? How do you guys build games so fast with this amazing graphics

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: I have an inspiration. I describe what I want in as much detail as I can and the models I selected generate concept art. I refine it with more prompting then pass it to an ai that can model. Then I have Astra rig it.

comments.author: KhaosPT
comments.body: Sometimes you need to tell opus exactly what is wrong. I sometimes find a scene and feed to Opus and tell it to analyse what patterns it finds that make the scenes be the scenes ( colors, camera position, style, number of objects, textures etc). And then for me the key was from another post here, I tell it to rate it's work 1 to 10 and iterate until it's 8.5 . But it really is not creative, you need to tell it what you want and what doesn't work, it won't one shot it for sure , not if you want quality

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: Use Opus 5.5 for Visual stuff. 3D Models and animations can be AAA Level if you have a workflow and good references. Generate Images and videos for your goal and the AI can replicate

comments.author: Big_Whale_95
comments.body:
Tripo3d or meshyai work both very good.   
[Here](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2rLQXDD9dY8) I show tripo in action

replies.author: AmazingTea1559
replies.body: I use Meshy for my assets, with chat gpt. The only thing is, if chat gpt gives you the front, sides and rear views just use the front view. Otherwise you'll end up with 4 models.

replies.author: Basic_Construction98
replies.body: that cool can i do it with claude or do i have to do it in thier ui? i want claude to do everything

replies.author: Big_Whale_95
replies.body: Not sure. I prefer their UI. so i have full control

comments.author: DudeWithASweater
comments.body:
Iterative prompts. Be explicit in your detail and give the model feedback as you go. Silo it's design to specific assets and features, instead of saying something like "build all my game assets, go!" Tell it" build this very specific asset in this specific way, use this refernece image as a guide, make it look like x, don't do this, etc".

Then when it comes back with an asset, get it to change things you don't like, expand on the things you do like, drop off features, add features, etc.

Iterate and then review.. and then interate some more.

comments.author: ThreeDMK
comments.body:
Currently using Opus to build scripts for my headless blender usage.  Trying to iterate on open world maps for race tracks.  It’s been interesting and a lot of compute and token usage, but the end result will mean much faster track generation down the road with less manual effort.

Like my software projects, I generally use AI to build tools so I can replicate actions consistently without AI, the same way I have done things in the past.  Instead of taking weeks to build something it just takes hours now.  :)
